# Synthetic SME dataset: FS1

**Entirely synthetic.** These are fictional profiles and invented monetary records generated by project code. They are not real companies, empirical SME evidence, a population sample, or a calibrated banking dataset. No external company data or personal records are used.

## Design and reproducibility

Generator version: `FS1`. Default fixed seed: **20261018**. Calendar history: **2024-01-01 through 2025-12-31**, inclusive (731 days per SME, including leap day). The current clock, locale, database IDs, and load timestamps do not enter canonical artifacts.

`SyntheticGenerator` uses Java `Random`, separate deterministic per-profile streams, integer minor-unit draws, and scale-2 BigDecimal values. The project remains on Java 17 with no new dependencies. Ordered generation, stable sorting, UTF-8, LF line endings, and Locale.ROOT formatting make artifacts repeatable. The generator-version namespace must change if generation semantics change; a golden fingerprint test detects unintended changes to FS1.

All three fictional SMEs use **USD** and two decimal places. There is no FX conversion or cross-currency comparison. Initial cash inputs are deliberately chosen constants, not estimated bank balances:

| Logical key | Fictional profile | Opening at start of 2024-01-01 | Invoices | Transactions | Daily rows | Closing on 2025-12-31 |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| FS1-20261018-A | Retail | 5000.00 | 314 | 1100 | 731 | 96934.82 |
| FS1-20261018-B | Agency | 12000.00 | 314 | 565 | 731 | 131432.78 |
| FS1-20261018-C | Workshop | 8000.00 | 314 | 849 | 731 | 149213.52 |

The default seed has **3 SMEs, 3 dated openings, 942 invoices, 2514 transactions, 932 linked payment transactions, and 2193 daily cash-flow rows**. Linked payments are included in the 2514 transactions, not extra cash rows. No scenarios or scenario inputs are generated. Different seeds can produce different transaction/payment counts; the manifest records each export's actual counts.

Opening balances remain in `opening_balances.csv`, keyed by logical SME and date. They are not inserted as transactions or stored in a new database table. The loader supplies them explicitly to the existing financial engine and prints the logical-key-to-live-ID mapping. This follows the accepted opening-cash design without a schema change.

## Invented generation assumptions

These are explicit example-design choices, not claims about real SME frequencies, costs, payment behavior, tax law, or sector seasonality:

- Two receivable invoices per week, on Tuesday and Friday; one payable on Wednesday. Dates are calendar dates without holiday or business-day adjustment.
- Due dates are issue date plus 14, 30, or 45 days, selected uniformly.
- Receivable base values are USD 400/1000/800 for retail/agency/workshop, plus a random 0 up to just under twice that base. Payables start at USD 150 plus a random 0 up to just under USD 450. Values then receive the stated seasonal factor.
- Monthly amount factors in percentage points are `[85,90,100,105,100,110,95,90,105,110,120,130]`; 2025 adds 5 percentage points. Scaling integer cents truncates fractional cents during synthetic amount creation. The financial engine itself never silently rounds amounts.
- Retail draws 0–2 direct sales per date; workshop 0–1; agency has no direct sales. Each sale starts at USD 50 plus a random 0 up to just under USD 250, scaled by the monthly factor. Weekends suppress the sale-count draw on 65% of dates; retained draws can still be zero.
- On weekdays, an operating expense occurs with a designed 35% probability, between USD 20 and just under USD 180.
- Rent on day 1 is USD 800/1200/1000 by profile. Payroll on day 25 is USD 2300/4300/3200 plus up to just under USD 200. An arbitrary TAX-labelled cash payment of USD 350 up to just under USD 600 occurs on day 20 of March/June/September/December. This is not a tax calculation or statutory schedule.
- Each invoice draws one of six equally likely designed payment modes: full 0–3 days before/on due date; full 3–21 days late; 40% seven days after issue then the remainder 3–14 days late; only 35% seven days after issue; no payment; or full 2–7 days after issue. Split components use integer cents and an exact remainder, so complete settlements equal face value.
- Scheduled payments after 2025-12-31 are omitted. Recent invoices are therefore right-censored: unpaid/partial at the cutoff does not mean permanent nonpayment or default. Persistent partial/unpaid modes are deliberate software exercise cases, not inferred bad-debt probabilities.

The default seed produces 593 PAID, 186 PARTIALLY_PAID, and 163 UNPAID invoices at the cutoff. Of fully settled invoices, 307 settled by/on due date and 286 settled late. There are 153 invoices with multiple observed payments and 316 outstanding invoices overdue at the cutoff. These counts include both receivables and payables; they are synthetic observations, not SME benchmarks.

## Payment consistency and cash treatment

The generator derives the stored invoice status from linked payments present through the dataset cutoff. Each link matches SME, currency, direction, and invoice reference; amounts are positive, exact cents, and never overpay an invoice. An issued invoice does not create an additional cash movement. Only its actual generated settlement transaction(s) affect cash. Direct sales are explicitly uninvoiced receipts; expenses, rent, payroll, and arbitrary tax payments have no invoice link.

`daily_cash_flow.csv` is the existing deterministic engine's roll-forward, including empty dates. Closing cash equals opening cash plus cumulative recorded inflows minus outflows. It is not a forecast. The default profiles have 178/316/221 empty dates respectively and no negative closing dates. This seed is not a liquidity stress dataset; existing engine tests cover negative cash and overpayments/cancellations that this dataset does not model.

## Export artifacts and labels

Default directory: `data/synthetic/FS1-20261018/`.

| File | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `smes.csv` | Fictional identities, logical keys, currency |
| `opening_balances.csv` | Three dated explicit opening inputs |
| `invoices.csv` | Face amounts, issue/due dates, direction, final-cutoff payment status |
| `transactions.csv` | Cash records, including optional invoice logical keys; all payments are here |
| `daily_cash_flow.csv` | Complete daily roll-forward per SME, with scale-2 money |
| `manifest.json` | Synthetic flag, seed/version/range/counts/units, SHA-256 of all five CSVs |

Every CSV row contains `is_synthetic=true`. Database names begin `SYNTHETIC FS1-...`, invoice references use the FS1 seed namespace, and every transaction description begins `SYNTHETIC` plus its logical key. Canonical artifacts exclude database identities and `created_at`, which naturally differ between fresh database loads.

Default full-artifact fingerprint (ordered file names/content, including manifest):

```text
d6751da8f13f5af6352ef126c637e14a6f67116a65ad665b8a628cd2cfa88e44
```

## Explicit commands

First build with PostgreSQL running and the existing test credentials exported:

```sh
set -a
source .env
set +a
MAVEN_USER_HOME="$PWD/.cache/maven" ./backend/mvnw -o -B -ntp -f backend/pom.xml -Dmaven.repo.local="$PWD/.cache/m2" verify
```

Then, from the repository root:

```sh
# File generation only; does not connect to PostgreSQL or require credentials.
./scripts/synthetic_data.sh generate --seed 20261018 --output data/synthetic/FS1-20261018
# Explicit development seeding; never runs at ordinary application startup.
./scripts/synthetic_data.sh load --seed 20261018
# Read-only verification of existing rows and engine results.
./scripts/synthetic_data.sh verify --seed 20261018
```

The wrapper selects a separate manual main class from the existing built JAR. It does not start Spring's web application or run migrations. Flyway migrations must already have been applied by normal application/test startup; follow database setup first. No global tools or new libraries are installed.

`load` and `verify` **regenerate from the specified seed and FS1 code**; they do not import arbitrary edited CSVs. Use matching seed/version for files and database. `--output` is accepted only for generation; relative paths are resolved from the repository root. The generated manifest and golden test are the reproducibility record.

The CLI accepts only a loopback JDBC URL for database `finsight` and role `finsight_app`, reads credentials from exported environment variables, and rejects superuser use. It does not print passwords. Tests construct the same loader against their separately guarded PostgreSQL datasource, not the development database.

## Repeatability and preservation

The generator checks every existing target before writing. Identical existing artifacts are accepted; changed artifacts are not overwritten. Interrupted exports can be completed by rerunning if existing files still match. Filesystem export is not a transactional database operation.

The loader acquires an advisory session lock before its REPEATABLE READ transaction snapshot, serializing cooperating loaders. It inserts SMEs, invoices, and cash movements in one transaction, then verifies complete content and financial-engine results before commit. Any failure rolls back its inserts (PostgreSQL identity sequences can still advance).

Rerunning `load` for a fully matching namespace returns the same live SME IDs and verifies it without inserting rows. A partial namespace, duplicate reserved name, changed invoice, missing/extra/modified transaction, or currency mismatch is an error; it never deletes, overwrites, or repairs existing data. Unrelated SMEs are not modified. There is no reset/delete command. Inspect a failed namespace before any manual correction; do not use seeding to replace real records.

Opening balances are external inputs: their canonical file/code/seed must be retained with the dataset. No database table stores their provenance. Reserved synthetic names are a tooling convention, not a new database uniqueness constraint. Unmanaged manual writers need not honor the advisory lock; concurrent-writer stress behavior was not tested.

## Future chronological experiments: boundaries and limits

731 ordered daily observations per SME support exercising a future chronological split and baseline pipeline; they do not establish statistical adequacy or real-world model performance. No train/test split, model training, forecast, or accuracy metric is implemented here.

For any future experiment, split by time and construct features only from data available by each cutoff. In particular, **`payment_status_at_cutoff` is the end-of-dataset snapshot and must not be used as a historical feature**. Use dated payments and the engine's as-of summaries instead. Future settlements, future daily closing balances, and whole-period aggregates also leak future information if used as past features. `created_at` is the load time, not a simulated historical arrival timestamp; the dataset does not model delayed ingestion.

All patterns, sector differences, growth, payment frequencies, and costs are invented. There are no real companies, account feeds, cancellations, refunds/reversals, FX, credit products, insolvency labels, or lending decisions. Synthetic results cannot validate real SME behavior or justify a banking decision. Source is the project's local generator; no external dataset is represented.

See `synthetic-data-verification.md` for actual test/load results.
